newsitem.title: USA: Lower equity offerings trim Interra Q2 net.
newsitem.headline: Lower equity offerings trim Interra Q2 net.

text.p: Interra Financial Inc said Wednesday its lower second quarter results were due to a reduction in equity offerings, which stalled underwriting and sales of stocks of small-to-medium-size companies.
"Our second-quarter and year-to-date results were off the record pace of 1996," said Chief Executive Irving Weiser.

"The higher-margin Equity Capital Markets businesses at Dain and Rauscher were impeded by the reduction in equity offerings, which stalled underwriting and sales of stocks of small-to-medium-size companies," he said in a news release.
Equity trading revenues were off sharply during the quarter, and revenues of its Private Client business were down slightly from the record first quarter, the company said.

Interra, parent company of regional securities firms Dain Bosworth of Minneapolis and Rauscher Pierce Refsnes of Dallas, reported second-quarter net earnings down 15 percent from a year earlier, although net revenues rose one percent.
The recent highs set by the large-stock indices such as the Dow industrials and S&P 500 belied lower trading volumes of smaller stocks during the second quarter, Weiser said.
"Fixed Income groups at Rauscher and Dain Bosworth had a relatively strong quarter," Weiser said.
Dain Bosworth's net revenues rose three percent to $101.5 million during the quarter. Pre-tax earnings fell 16 percent to $11.2 million.
Rauscher's net revenues dropped five percent to $45.8 million in the quarter. Its pre-tax earnings fell 30 percent to $4.8 million.

Interra expanded its operations during the second quarter. Dain added 11 to its staff in Minneapolis and New York, and added retail offices in Bainbridge Island, Wash., near Seattle, and Fort Collins, Colo. Rauscher opened a retail office in New Orleans and added six fixed-income staff members in New York.
